Source commit 62d7f72aa00f3d09aa6ec1240e0191b6904de2b2, build_id 2e4524529ac0896385ce43eece6c313d19beb611a4af69da66e37fd889e33bea, Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, Forward+. beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW - Claude UI cold open. The prompt is an ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION of the walker ask, never a transcript.
beats.narration_text: Merhaba, this is Liam, in for Bear. The ask, reconstructed: in Mimic Keep, an archer on a castle wall shoots fire arrows at straw scarecrows. Give the scarecrows a walk cycle from a sprite sheet, and give the archer a shot that draws, releases and recovers.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Mimic Keep, a castle-defense game where an archer on the wall shoots fire arrows at straw scarecrows, into two animations: a looping scarecrow walk from a sprite sheet, and an archer shot on a keyed cutout rig, driven by a state machine. I write the brief, the phase table, every prediction and verdict; agents build and test; I judge the motion in play.

beats.role_note: What was built, with one real correction: the full-draw key went from -8 to -16 degrees after Rui's look.
beats.narration_text: Two clips. Rui wrote the brief and the phase table; agent sessions built the keys, the state machine and the tests. The tests proved the structure. Only Rui's eyes could say the draw was too small, so eight degrees became sixteen.

beats.role_note: The game and both clips in play.
beats.narration_text: This is the game, with nobody at the keys. The scarecrows walk down on a four cell cycle, and the one outside the archer's reach stops at the wall. The archer draws, releases and recovers on its own, one shot every point six seconds.

beats.role_note: Both clips, their routes, which loops and which commits, and the one authority over each.
beats.narration_text: The brief names both clips. The scarecrow walk is the cycle: a Sprite2D sliced four by one, keyed by an AnimationPlayer frame track. The archer's shot is the committing action: a three part cutout rig, keyed in the scene file and played by an AnimationTree state machine. Each has exactly one authority.

props.title: Two clips, two routes, one authority each

beats.role_note: Q1: what a clip is, pointed at the walk clip's own lines; the frame track that reads the sheet.
beats.narration_text: What is a clip? This one. An Animation resource holding tracks. A track names a node and a property: sprite, colon, frame. Four keys at zero, point one two five, point two five and point three seven five seconds set the integers zero to three. Update one is discrete, so each frame holds. Nothing here knows about scarecrows.

props.title: What a clip is: a list of keys.
props.source: Verbatim project source at commit 62d7f72 · Godot editor reconstruction (teaching view)

tracks/0/imported = false

tracks/0/path = NodePath("Sprite:frame")
tracks/0/interp = 1
tracks/0/loop_wrap = true
tracks/0/keys = {
"times": PackedFloat32Array(0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375),
"transitions": PackedFloat32Array(1, 1, 1, 1),

beats.role_note: The sheet, its 4×1 slicing, and the walk strip's cells.
beats.narration_text: Which cell is frame three is decided by the slicing, h frames four, not by the image. The sheet is written by code, so no third party licence applies. In the walk preview a camera holds the scarecrow still: its pole foot stays in one column, and hops zero, minus three, plus one, minus three pixels.

shot.label: Fixture capture · walk_preview, camera follows the scarecrow

beats.role_note: Q1: a track that names a missing property is silently inert.
beats.narration_text: And why a wrong property fails silently. Mutation one renamed the property to frames. The scene still loads with no error, and the track would key nothing. Only the read-back saw it: no property called frames on a Sprite2D.

beats.role_note: Q4: feel designed in frames; the phase table beside the key times built from it.
beats.narration_text: Feel is designed in frames. Rui counted a real archer, converted to thirty frames per second: twenty six frames of draw, one of loose, fourteen of follow through. The game compresses that to eight, one and six, at a step of one thirtieth of a second. The key times come from that table, not the other way round.

props.title: The phase table, then the keys
props.excerpt: Frame rate: 30 fps. `Animation.step` = 1/30 s (one frame period). Clip length 15 frames = 0.5 s.

beats.role_note: The committing action keyed at its phase boundaries, verbatim.
beats.narration_text: The keys, built from the table. Step is one thirtieth. The bow's rotation is keyed at frames zero, eight, nine and fifteen. Transition two accelerates into full draw; point five settles through recovery. The full draw value is minus sixteen degrees, after tuning. The same clip keys release window, true for one frame.

beats.role_note: The frame strip at each phase boundary, with the log line for each frame.
beats.narration_text: The fixture strip at each boundary. Frame ten is the trigger, still looking idle. Eighteen is full draw, release window true, no arrow yet. Nineteen: the arrow is out, because the archer reads the key one tick after the tree writes it. Twenty five is idle again.

beats.role_note: The observation-driven revision: observation, prediction, two strips, verdict.
beats.narration_text: The revision came from Rui's eyes, not Claude's. Rui watched first: the draw moved too little, and the phases were hard to tell apart. The agent proposed one key, minus eight degrees to minus sixteen, and predicted every logged angle. The log matched; one frame missed, on unseeded particles. Rui kept it, and in play said the three phases read clearly.

beats.role_note: Q2 one authority and Q3 two clocks, pointed at the archer's own lines.
beats.narration_text: One authority. Only the AnimationTree writes release window, keyed in the clip. The archer reads it here, in physics process, and never writes it. Two clocks: the tree's callback mode is physics, so the clip and this read share a tick type. The scarecrow's player runs on idle, and no gameplay reads it.

props.title: One authority, one clock.
props.source: Verbatim project source at commit 62d7f72 · Godot editor reconstruction (teaching view)

startup only: a lost target cancels

beats.role_note: Q3 measured: one physics tick between the key and the read.
beats.narration_text: Measured, from the same windowed run as the strip: release window turns true on tick thirty seven, and the arrow fires on tick thirty eight. The largest disagreement is one physics tick, a sixtieth of a second, already inside the point three second draw lead.

shot.label: Fixture capture · log lines from the same windowed run

beats.role_note: Q2 for the sprite: the presenter only picks the clip; the AnimationPlayer is the one writer.
beats.narration_text: The walk's authority. The presenter reads at wall and picks walk or hold. It never writes the frame: the AnimationPlayer is the frame's only writer. It compares the assigned animation, because a one key hold clip empties current animation when it ends.

props.title: The walk's one writer.

beats.role_note: The state machine in real play, with an interrupt in each phase.
beats.narration_text: Interrupts in each phase, keys sent by a script into the real game. P in startup freezes the bow half drawn; P again, and it finishes and fires. P on the active frame holds full draw; on resume the arrow leaves. P in recovery freezes the swing back. Moving does not interrupt. A target at the wall, walked out of the cone, cancels the draw: no arrow.

beats.role_note: What the read-backs proved, the mutations, what no headless run shows.
beats.narration_text: What the tests proved. Both read-backs pass, sixty eight and one sixty six checks. The state machine test, one oh seven, drives real keys. The edge test, three twenty five, hits every boundary before, on and after. The pins pass again. Mutations one to three failed their read-backs; four passed, as a keyed rig should. No headless run draws a frame, so none of this says the motion reads.

shot.label: Recorded output · test logs and mutations

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught, Claude's readings overruled, what remains uncertain.
beats.narration_text: Mistakes caught. An agent reported seventy two checks where there were sixty eight, and mistyped a log line. Claude's own helper fix fired no arrow, and its playtest checklist was wrong: walking away cancels a draw only near the wall. Rui overruled the agent's minus eight degrees. Still uncertain: no human has seen a startup cancel.

props.title: Caught, overruled, uncertain

beats.role_note: Verdict: shown, checked, uncertain, next step, contributions, sheet source and licence, source revision.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Shown working: a clean walk cycle, and a shot whose phases read in play. Limits: a startup cancel comes too early to see, and the fixture and the game disagree on the phases. Next: a larger release kick, so recovery reads. Rui wrote the brief, the table, every verdict and capture. Claude and the agents built and tested the rest.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the paste ready prompt. Write your phase table in frames before any key exists. Let an agent key it and read it back, then judge the motion in the running game yourself, because no test can see it. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Use Walker. I will write one committing action's phase table in frames, with the frame rate and Animation.step, before any key exists. Key it at every phase boundary, add a read-back that pins the times with a half-frame tolerance, and give me a fixture preview to capture. I judge the motion in the running game.
